prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S096: The Field Supervisor coordinates task execution offshore and keeps the Duty Planner informed of changes to work progress.
S097: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S098: The operating organization uses defined handoffs so that dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision, and stores control remain accountable functions.
S099: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S100: This section defines how offshore environmental observations and protected operational networks support safe farm operations.
S101: The Metocean Buoy is designated Copper Finch for operational reference.
S102: The Metocean Buoy measures wind speed and direction, wave height and period, current, air temperature, and barometric pressure.
S103: Sensors are selected and mounted to limit exposure to spray, icing, vibration, and corrosion.
S104: An onboard logger timestamps observations and retains a local history during intermittent communications.
S105: The Vessel AIS Receiver produces a Position Quality Flag when position integrity checks fail or confidence falls below its configured threshold.
S106: The Weather Service uses validated environmental observations in forecast products for offshore planning.
S107: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast limitations and identifies conditions that may affect vessel access or turbine work.
S108: Measurement intervals and alarm thresholds are configured to support both trend analysis and timely operational decisions.
S109: Time synchronization and sensor health are checked as part of routine monitoring.
S110: The Cybersecurity Gateway is designated Quiet Harbor for operational reference.
S111: The Cybersecurity Gateway establishes a controlled boundary between authorized shore-side services and offshore operational networks.
S112: The boundary permits only approved protocols, destinations, and service accounts.
S113: External connectivity is denied by default and enabled only for documented operational needs.
S114: The SCADA Gateway remains responsible for supervisory communications within its defined control scope.
S115: Administrative access requires authenticated individual accounts and role-based authorization.
S116: Privileged sessions are time limited, logged, and reviewed against approved maintenance activity.
S117: The Cybersecurity Analyst monitors gateway events for unusual access patterns and configuration changes.
S118: Loss of the security boundary places remote administrative functions in a restricted state without bypassing local protective controls.
S119: Security events are retained in protected logs for investigation and audit.
S120: Network segmentation limits the effect of a compromised endpoint and supports controlled restoration of service.
S121: Interfaces are tested after configuration changes to confirm that permitted functions remain available and prohibited paths remain blocked.
S122: Operational procedures identify the authority for approving access, responding to alarms, and returning affected services to normal operation.
S123: This section describes turbine control and remote observation during offshore operations.
S124: Vessel AIS Receiver is designated Blue Granite for this operational concept.
S125: Blade Inspection Drone is designated Larkspur for this operational concept.
S126: Duty Planner prepares the Transfer Manifest Addendum to capture approved vessel deployment changes.
S127: Glassfin adjusts turbine output within approved operating limits and blocks commands that conflict with active protection conditions.
S128: Pale Lantern issues forecast updates that support timing decisions for remote observation and field work.
S129: Turbine Controller executes authorized control actions and reports its operating state through established control interfaces.
S130: Pitch System changes blade angle in response to turbine control commands and local protection logic.
S131: Converter Cabinet manages electrical conversion while observing equipment limits and protective interlocks.
S132: Nacelle Condition Monitor provides equipment measurements for ongoing assessment of turbine health.
S133: SCADA Gateway presents turbine status and control availability to authorized shore personnel.
S134: Shore Control Room provides a staffed location for supervisory control and operational review.
S135: Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating conditions before issuing a remote command.
S136: Remote commands are subject to role-based authorization and are recorded for later operational review.
S137: Local protection functions retain priority when remote requests conflict with safe operating limits.
S138: Control availability is checked before remote operation begins and after relevant configuration changes.
S139: Vessel AIS Receiver collects vessel position broadcasts to support marine traffic awareness.
S140: The receiver maintains a time-stamped view of nearby vessel movements when broadcast coverage is available.
S141: Marine Coordinator uses the available traffic picture to support coordination of offshore movements.
S142: Blade Inspection Drone captures close-range visual observations of accessible blade surfaces.
S143: Blade Specialist plans inspection passes to provide consistent coverage of areas selected for examination.
S144: Captured imagery is reviewed for visible surface changes and potential maintenance concerns.
S145: Field Supervisor considers remote observations alongside site conditions before recommending follow-up work.
S146: Drone operation is suspended when weather, visibility, or equipment status makes flight unsafe.
S147: Remote observations supplement field assessment and do not replace required physical inspections.
S148: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.
S149: Work Permit Portal is the controlled entry point for planning, reviewing, approving, and closing maintenance work.
